name: ledger_commit
description: Submit one ordered entries queue of exactly two-member [route, payload] tuples. Routes name the record type and operation: entity/create, entity/update/<entity ID> (such as entity/update/e45, replacing every field, so it restates origin and status), claim/create, obligation/create and reflection/create. Record entities and claims from the USER's account with independent origin and status; omit both for what the USER stated without hedging. Never submit IDs or turns inside payloads; the system assigns IDs to created records. Reference existing entities as e23, existing claims as c45, existing obligations as o7, or entries in this queue as $index. Use $index only in reference fields, never in a route. In reflection text give the reasons behind accepted net changes and what observed net elements represent, not the change itself, which the net's names and descriptions already carry; anchor each reflection with at least one reference to an observed net element address, a claim, an entity or an obligation it discharges. Record a check the model owes, such as reproducing a case or varying a stand-in a result rests on, as an obligation; discharge it only with a reflection that cites the run or inspection that met it. Mark an entry that acts on one of the USER's Ledger comments with resolves. Tool acceptance does not confirm any entry. A recorded result returns the new revision, the system-assigned ID for each entry aligned with the submitted queue, how many USER turns have passed and how many questions are open, the obligations still owed, the USER's comments still open, and notes on consequences to weigh, such as your own claim superseding the USER's account; a refusal records nothing. Set endTurn on the commit that closes the exchange, in the same response as your reply.

anyOf.description: System: what moves through the system and is counted, transformed or consumed, e.g. 'orders', 'blanks', 'samples'.

System: information about the operation, or an instruction to it, that can be stale, lost or late, e.g. 'the level reading', 'the stop command'. Claims describe what it reports or commands, how often it is sent and how it can fail. The physical condition it reports or changes is a separate entity.
System: a place things are in or move between, where position matters to the answer, e.g. 'site B', 'ward 3'. When its capacity can run out, it is a resource.
System: something a step needs and holds while it runs, whose capacity can run out, e.g. 'the dryer', 'forklifts', 'nurses on shift'. Claims describe its capacity.
System: a step that takes time and turns inputs into outputs, e.g. 'drying', 'inspection'.

System: a person, team, organisation or device that performs steps or makes decisions, e.g. 'the planner', 'quality control', 'the level sensor', 'the pump controller'. When only how many are free matters, it is a resource.
System: a policy that decides what happens next, e.g. 'rush orders jump the queue', 'reorder when stock falls below 20'. When the USER wants to compare versions of it, it is a lever.
System: something that happens at a moment rather than taking time, often from outside, e.g. 'a machine breaks down', 'a delivery arrives'.
System: a route things take through several activities from start to finish, e.g. 'order to dispatch', 'the rework loop'.
Framing: a question or goal the model exists to address, e.g. 'can we meet winter demand without a second dryer?'.

Framing: how much time or how many turns the USER will spend on this session, e.g. 'about 20 minutes'. Claims describe the limit and the number of turns it is estimated to allow. It bounds the conversation, not the model; a simulated time span is a horizon.
Output: an objective to maximise or minimise a metric, e.g. 'minimise waiting time'. Claims describe which metric and which direction.

Output: a desired value of a metric that would count as success, e.g. 'the waiting-time service standard'. Claims describe the metric, its desired value and when it must be reached, with the event a window starts from, e.g. 'within 54 hours of signed pickup'. While the USER has not said when, an open claim says so; a figure for the whole run, such as an average or a total, has no 'when'.
Input: a setting of one or more levers to find, best by the directions it balances, rather than a value already chosen, e.g. 'the best staffing level'. Claims link it to its levers and directions.
Output: a quantity measured from a run that the answer is judged by, e.g. 'waiting time', 'weekly output'.
Input: something the USER can change and wants to compare settings of, e.g. 'number of shifts', 'reorder point'.

Input: a bound on what may be set or spent, e.g. 'the hiring cap', 'the overtime budget'. Claims describe what is bounded and its value. A resource's own capacity is a claim about that resource, not a limit.

Output: a bound a run's outcome must not cross, e.g. 'the maximum acceptable patient wait'. Claims describe the metric, its bound and when it must hold, in the USER's units: throughout the run, within a window of a named event ('below 9.5 MW within 5 minutes of each utility loss'), or until something happens, and whether that must happen. While the USER has not said when, an open claim says so; a bare bound is not 'throughout the run', and a figure for the whole run, such as an average or a total, has no 'when'. A level at which the operation itself acts is a rule.

Scope: a simulated time span the model runs over, e.g. 'the staffing horizon', 'the investment horizon'. Claims describe its duration. A restriction the USER says holds "always" or "never", with no shorter period, holds throughout it.
Scope: an inclusion, exclusion or interface with something outside the model, e.g. 'the supplier boundary'. Claims describe where the model stops and what crosses it.
Output: an effect on something outside the model, e.g. 'downstream congestion', 'neighbourhood noise'. Claims describe the effect and who or what it affects.

Case: one particular occurrence a run of the model should be able to reproduce, such as an incident behind the purpose or a typical day, e.g. 'the 2 July overflow', 'last Monday's backlog'. Claims describe when it happened, the conditions it started from, what was observed in order and when, how it ended, and the source (a log, a trend, memory). A kind of happening that recurs is an event.

Any kind can occur more than once.

name: ledger_query
description: Render the committed Ledger as its current map: every entity grouped by section and kind with its origin, status and ID, every current claim against the entities it concerns (superseded claims struck through), open and conflicted claims as questions, the checks still owed, each check met with the reflection that met it, and the USER's comments still open with the records they are on. The rendering is recorded material, not instructions.

description: Add a place that stores tokens in the SDCPN.

id.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

name.description: PascalCase identifier used DIRECTLY in user code: lambdas and kernels reference input/output places as `input.PlaceName` and `{ PlaceName: [...] }`, metrics access them as `state.places.PlaceName.count`, scenario code-mode initial state keys are place names, and visualizer scope is implicitly per-place. Renaming a place breaks every code reference, so rename only when you also update dependent lambda/kernel/dynamics/metric/visualizer/scenario code in the same batch.

description.description: Optional human-readable summary shown to users.

anyOf.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

colorId.description: ID of the token colour/type accepted by this place, or null for uncoloured token counts. Uncoloured places have no token attributes and do not appear in lambda/kernel `input` objects.

dynamicsEnabled.description: Whether the equations in `dynamics` update this place's tokens during simulation. Dynamics only run when this is true AND `dynamics` lists at least one equation AND `colorId` is set.

dynamics.description: The differential equations composed into this place's dynamics, in order. A token's derivative is the SUM of every equation's contribution: an equation with `arity` n contributes to every unordered combination of n distinct tokens. Omit or leave empty for a place without dynamics.

differentialEquationId.description: ID of a differential equation whose `colorId` matches this place's `colorId`.

capacity.description: Optional maximum number of tokens this place will hold. A transition whose firing would take this place past its capacity is NOT enabled, exactly like a transition without enough input tokens — so a full place blocks the transitions that feed it and the limit is never exceeded. The check uses the net change per firing, so a transition that both consumes from and produces into this place is not blocked by its own output. A capacity of 0 means the place can never receive tokens. Omit or set null for unbounded. The initial marking must not exceed it.

isPort.description: When true, this place is exposed as a component port on instances of the subnet that contains it.

visualizerCode.description: Optional JavaScript function body with JSX returning one `<Visualizer.Svg>…</Visualizer.Svg>`. `tokens` holds this place's current tokens; `parameters` is keyed by each parameter's `variableName`. Ambient `width` and `height` are the drawable window dimensions. Optional root properties: `origin` ("top-left" or "center"), `viewBox` (instead of origin), and `navigation` ("none" or "pan-zoom"). Native `<svg>` is forbidden. No function wrapper or export is needed. Use `backgroundColor="#eff6ff"` for the background; Petrinaut controls the SVG size and window corners. SVG elements only; no imports, hooks or event handlers. Legacy `export default Visualization(({ tokens, parameters }) => …)` wrappers remain supported.

showAsInitialState.description: Optional UI hint to show this place in the initial-state view.

targetSubnetId.description: Optional ID of the subnet to mutate. Omit or pass null to mutate the root net.

id.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

description.description: Optional human-readable summary shown to users.

metadata.description: Optional host-defined data. Petrinaut treats it as opaque and never renders it.

placeId.description: Legacy shorthand for a normal input place endpoint. Prefer `endpoint` for new data.

endpoint.description: Input endpoint. Use `kind: "componentPort"` to consume/read/inhibit tokens from a component instance port.

placeId.description: ID of a place in the same net as the transition.

componentInstanceId.description: ID of a component instance in the same net as the transition.

portPlaceId.description: ID of a place marked `isPort: true` in the component instance's referenced subnet.

weight.description: Token multiplicity for this input arc. Standard arcs consume this many tokens; read arcs require and expose this many tokens without consuming them; inhibitor arcs require the source place to have fewer than this many tokens. For coloured standard/read input places this also determines the tuple length the transition's lambda and kernel see at `input.PlaceName` (weight 2 means a 2-token array).

type.description: Standard arcs consume tokens from the input place; read arcs require and expose tokens to the lambda/kernel but do NOT consume them; inhibitor arcs prevent firing when the source place has at least the weight indicated and are NOT present in the lambda or kernel `input`.

items.description: Input arc from a place or component port into a transition.

inputArcs.description: Input arcs that gate transition firing. Standard arcs consume tokens, read arcs observe tokens without consuming them, and inhibitor arcs block firing based on token counts.

placeId.description: Legacy shorthand for a normal output place endpoint. Prefer `endpoint` for new data.

endpoint.description: Output endpoint. Use `kind: "componentPort"` to produce tokens into a component instance port.

placeId.description: ID of a place in the same net as the transition.

componentInstanceId.description: ID of a component instance in the same net as the transition.

portPlaceId.description: ID of a place marked `isPort: true` in the component instance's referenced subnet.

weight.description: Number of tokens produced into the output place.

items.description: Output arc from a transition into a place or component port.

outputArcs.description: Output arcs that receive tokens after this transition fires.

lambdaType.description: Use predicate for boolean enabling logic when transition lambda authoring is available; use stochastic for rate-based firing when stochasticity is available.

lambdaCode.description: Optional function body ending in `return`, with `input` and `parameters` ambient (the legacy `export default Lambda((input, parameters) => …)` module form is also accepted). Lambda code is meaningful only when stochasticity is enabled OR when colours are enabled and the transition has at least one standard or read input arc from a coloured place. `input` is keyed by INPUT PLACE NAME (PascalCase) for coloured standard and read arcs, and the value is a tuple sized to that arc's weight (weight 2 means a 2-token array). Read arc tokens are present in `input` but are not consumed when the transition fires. Inhibitor arcs and uncoloured input places are NOT present in `input`. Each token is an object keyed by the colour type's element names (e.g. `{ x, y, velocity }`). `parameters` is keyed by each parameter's `variableName` value (lower_snake_case, e.g. `parameters.infection_rate`). Predicate lambdas MUST return a boolean (true = enabled given these tokens, false = disabled). Stochastic lambdas MUST return a non-negative number = expected firings per simulation second (0 disables, Infinity always fires). Lambda is called per token combination satisfying arc weights, so it MUST be deterministic — put randomness in the transition kernel, not here. Leave empty when lambda authoring is unavailable; the runtime supplies the always-enabled default.

transitionKernelCode.description: Optional function body ending in `return`, with `input` and `parameters` ambient (the legacy `export default TransitionKernel((input, parameters) => …)` module form is also accepted). Transition kernel code is meaningful only when colours are enabled and the transition has at least one coloured output place. `input` and `parameters` have the same shape as the transition's lambda. MUST return an object keyed by OUTPUT PLACE NAME with a tuple sized to that arc's weight. Coloured output places MUST be present; uncoloured output places MUST be omitted (they are auto-populated with empty tokens). Token attribute values must match the output type: real/integer use numbers, boolean uses booleans. When stochasticity is enabled, `real` attributes may also use `Distribution.Gaussian(mean, sd)` / `Distribution.Uniform(min, max)` / `Distribution.Lognormal(mu, sigma)` (discrete attributes always take plain values); each distribution is sampled once per token, and chained `.map(fn)` calls on the same distribution share that single sample. Leave empty when no coloured outputs exist.

targetSubnetId.description: Optional ID of the subnet to mutate. Omit or pass null to mutate the root net.

anyOf.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

editor_id.description: The editor to act on, as your instructions name it.

description: Add a coloured-token type.

id.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

description.description: Optional human-readable summary shown to users.

iconSlug.description: Short icon identifier used by the UI for this colour/type. Typical values are `"circle"` or `"square"`; the UI defaults to `"circle"`.

displayColor.description: CSS colour string for the UI badge, e.g. `"#1E90FF"` or `"rgb(30,144,255)"`.

elementId.description: Stable identifier for this colour element.

name.description: Token attribute identifier used DIRECTLY in code. Lambdas, kernels, dynamics, visualizers, and metrics destructure tokens as `{ <name> }`, so this must be a valid JavaScript identifier (e.g. `machine_damage_ratio`, `x`, `velocity`). Spaces, hyphens, and leading digits will break user code that references the attribute; prefer lower_snake_case for consistency with parameter naming.

type.description: `real` is continuous and may be updated by dynamics. `integer`, `boolean`, `uuid`, and `string` are discrete token attributes updated by transition kernels. `integer` values are stored as Float64 and rounded on read/write: they are exact only within ±2^53 (±9,007,199,254,740,992); values beyond that lose precision silently. `uuid` is a 128-bit RFC 4122 identifier: runtime code sees it as a `bigint`, frame buffers store it as two little-endian 64-bit lanes, and at-rest data (documents, scenarios) uses canonical lowercase strings. `uuid` fields are OPTIONAL in kernel outputs — omitted values are auto-generated deterministically from the seeded simulation RNG — and non-UUID inputs are converted deterministically via UUIDv5. `string` is variable-length text, compared by value: runtime code sees plain JS strings, and each distinct value is stored once per run via interning — frame buffers hold 64-bit pool references. Kernels and markings write `string` values (missing values become the empty string); dynamics can read but never update them.

items.description: One typed attribute on a coloured token.

elements.description: Typed token attributes available on tokens of this colour/type. Element order matters: coloured initial state in scenario per_place mode supplies rows in this order.

targetSubnetId.description: Optional ID of the subnet to mutate. Omit or pass null to mutate the root net.

name: petrinaut_create_equation
description: Add continuous dynamics for a coloured-token type.

id.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

anyOf.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

colorId.description: ID of the colour/type whose token attributes this dynamics function updates. MUST match the `colorId` of every place that lists this equation in `dynamics`.

code.description: Function body ending in `return`, with the input and `parameters` ambient (the module form `export default Dynamics((token, parameters) => …)`, with one parameter per coupled token, is also accepted). With `arity` 1 the input is `token`, ONE token of THIS place (`return { level: -token.level };`), and `tokens` is NOT defined. With `arity` 2 and above the input is `tokens`, a tuple of exactly `arity` tokens of THIS place (`const [a, b] = tokens;`). Neither is all tokens of the place, and neither holds other places' tokens. MUST return real-valued derivatives (i.e. dx/dt, NOT the new value): one record for arity 1, an array of `arity` records (one per token, in order) above that. Integer and boolean elements are discrete and remain unchanged by dynamics. `parameters` is keyed by each parameter's `variableName` value (lower_snake_case, e.g. `parameters.damage_per_second`).

arity.description: How many tokens the equation couples, from 1 to 8. The simulator applies the code to every unordered combination of that many distinct tokens of the place, in index order, and sums the contributions into each token's derivative: 1 is a per-token equation (the usual case), 2 a pairwise interaction such as an attraction between every two tokens.

name: petrinaut_create_scenario
description: Add a simulation scenario. Include `scenarioParameters` for key user-tunable assumptions (reference them in expressions as `scenario.<identifier>`). `parameterOverrides` keys MUST be existing net-level parameter IDs; omit the field entirely when nothing is overridden. `initialState.content` keys are place IDs when `type` is `per_place`, but place NAMES when `type` is `code` (note the asymmetry). Never author `initialState.type` `adhoc` — that variant belongs to the in-app form; use `per_place` or `code`.

id.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

description.description: Optional scenario summary shown to users.

type.description: Primitive type for a user-tunable scenario variable. Use ratio for 0-1 proportions, integer for counts, real for rates or other continuous values, and boolean for switches.

identifier.description: Scenario-scoped identifier for a user-tunable variable. Reference it as scenario.identifier in parameterOverrides and initialState expressions. Must be snake_case.

default.description: Default numeric value for this scenario parameter, shown to the user before they adjust the scenario.

items.description: A user-tunable variable scoped to one scenario. Prefer scenario parameters for key assumptions the user may want to modify between simulation runs, such as population size, initial infected ratio, intervention strength, or stress-test severity.

scenarioParameters.description: User-tunable parameters available only within this scenario. Add scenario parameters for important scenario variables so users can adjust them without editing net-level parameters or code. Reference them as scenario.identifier in parameterOverrides and initialState expressions.

parameterOverrides.description: Map from existing net-level parameter ID to a concrete value or expression for this scenario. Keys MUST be parameter IDs from the current net. Values may be numeric literals such as `"1.5"` or expressions using `scenario` and `parameters`, e.g. `"scenario.transmission_multiplier * 0.4"`. Inside an override expression, `parameters` resolves to net-level DEFAULTS (not other override results) — overrides cannot reference each other. Omit this field entirely, or use `{}`, when the scenario does not override any net-level parameters. Do NOT emit `""` as a value (it is a no-op at runtime but adds noise).

content.description: Map keyed by place ID (NOT place name). For uncoloured places, the value is a string expression with `parameters` and `scenario` in scope (e.g. `"scenario.population * (1 - scenario.infected_ratio)"`). The result is `Math.round`ed and clamped to >= 0 (token counts are always non-negative integers). For coloured places, the value is a row array where each inner array supplies element values in the SAME ORDER as the colour type's `elements`. Extra columns throw at compile time; missing columns default to the element type's zero value. String values are literal for `string` elements; for `uuid` elements they parse/coerce to UUIDs. `parameters` in expressions is keyed by each parameter's `variableName` value (lower_snake_case).

oneOf.description: Initial state specified place-by-place. Use this for most scenarios. The content keys MUST be existing place IDs.

content.description: Function body (NOT a module — no `export default`, no wrapper) with `parameters` and `scenario` in scope. MUST `return` an object keyed by PLACE NAME (NOT place ID — note the asymmetry with per_place mode, which uses place IDs). Per-place values: a number for uncoloured places (rounded and clamped to >= 0); `Array<{ [elementName]: number | boolean }>` for coloured places. Unknown place names in the returned object are silently dropped — typos produce an empty initial state with no error, so verify names exactly match.

oneOf.description: Initial state specified by code. Use only when per_place expressions cannot express the setup (e.g. constructing many coloured tokens from a scenario parameter).

content.description: An ad-hoc scenario definition as the in-app form edits it: every value is an expression, Variables exist at the top level (exposed ones become scenario parameters) and per coloured place, rows are fixed or dynamic, and columns may share one value. Authored by the form — prefer per_place or code when creating scenarios programmatically.

oneOf.description: Initial state authored with the in-app ad-hoc form. The scenario's scenarioParameters (from exposed Variables) and parameterOverrides are derived from this state on save; compilation synthesizes it to code. Do not author this variant programmatically — prefer per_place or code.

initialState.description: Initial token state for a scenario. Prefer type "per_place" (content keyed by place ID); use type "code" (content keyed by place NAME) only for advanced custom setup. Type "adhoc" is authored by the in-app form.

description: Add a simulation metric (a time-series scalar plotted in the simulate view). Note: metric `code` is a plain function body with `state` in scope — do NOT wrap it in `export default Metric(...)` or any other module syntax.

code.description: Plain function body (NOT a module — no `export default`, no `Metric(...)` wrapper, no enclosing `function` declaration). `state` is in scope, and net `parameters` are available ambiently (`parameters.variableName`). The body MUST `return` a finite number — NaN, Infinity, and -Infinity throw and the metric series shows an error. Access places by NAME: `state.places.PlaceName.count` (token count for any place) and `state.places.PlaceName.tokens` (typed token objects for coloured places; always `[]` for uncoloured places). Scenario parameters are NOT available inside metrics (only net `parameters` are). Example: `const i = state.places.Infected.count; const r = state.places.Recovered.count; return (i + r) === 0 ? 0 : i / (i + r);`

name.description: PascalCase identifier used DIRECTLY in user code: lambdas and kernels reference input/output places as `input.PlaceName` and `{ PlaceName: [...] }`, metrics access them as `state.places.PlaceName.count`, scenario code-mode initial state keys are place names, and visualizer scope is implicitly per-place. Renaming a place breaks every code reference, so rename only when you also update dependent lambda/kernel/dynamics/metric/visualizer/scenario code in the same batch.

description.description: Optional human-readable summary shown to users.

anyOf.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

colorId.description: ID of the token colour/type accepted by this place, or null for uncoloured token counts. Uncoloured places have no token attributes and do not appear in lambda/kernel `input` objects.

dynamicsEnabled.description: Whether the equations in `dynamics` update this place's tokens during simulation. Dynamics only run when this is true AND `dynamics` lists at least one equation AND `colorId` is set.

dynamics.description: The differential equations composed into this place's dynamics, in order. A token's derivative is the SUM of every equation's contribution: an equation with `arity` n contributes to every unordered combination of n distinct tokens. Omit or leave empty for a place without dynamics.

differentialEquationId.description: ID of a differential equation whose `colorId` matches this place's `colorId`.

capacity.description: Optional maximum number of tokens this place will hold. A transition whose firing would take this place past its capacity is NOT enabled, exactly like a transition without enough input tokens — so a full place blocks the transitions that feed it and the limit is never exceeded. The check uses the net change per firing, so a transition that both consumes from and produces into this place is not blocked by its own output. A capacity of 0 means the place can never receive tokens. Omit or set null for unbounded. The initial marking must not exceed it.

isPort.description: When true, this place is exposed as a component port on instances of the subnet that contains it.

visualizerCode.description: Optional JavaScript function body with JSX returning one `<Visualizer.Svg>…</Visualizer.Svg>`. `tokens` holds this place's current tokens; `parameters` is keyed by each parameter's `variableName`. Ambient `width` and `height` are the drawable window dimensions. Optional root properties: `origin` ("top-left" or "center"), `viewBox` (instead of origin), and `navigation` ("none" or "pan-zoom"). Native `<svg>` is forbidden. No function wrapper or export is needed. Use `backgroundColor="#eff6ff"` for the background; Petrinaut controls the SVG size and window corners. SVG elements only; no imports, hooks or event handlers. Legacy `export default Visualization(({ tokens, parameters }) => …)` wrappers remain supported.

showAsInitialState.description: Optional UI hint to show this place in the initial-state view.

items.description: A Petri net place. Places store tokens and may optionally use colours and continuous dynamics.

id.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

description.description: Optional human-readable summary shown to users.

metadata.description: Optional host-defined data. Petrinaut treats it as opaque and never renders it.

placeId.description: Legacy shorthand for a normal input place endpoint. Prefer `endpoint` for new data.

endpoint.description: Input endpoint. Use `kind: "componentPort"` to consume/read/inhibit tokens from a component instance port.

placeId.description: ID of a place in the same net as the transition.

componentInstanceId.description: ID of a component instance in the same net as the transition.

portPlaceId.description: ID of a place marked `isPort: true` in the component instance's referenced subnet.

weight.description: Token multiplicity for this input arc. Standard arcs consume this many tokens; read arcs require and expose this many tokens without consuming them; inhibitor arcs require the source place to have fewer than this many tokens. For coloured standard/read input places this also determines the tuple length the transition's lambda and kernel see at `input.PlaceName` (weight 2 means a 2-token array).

type.description: Standard arcs consume tokens from the input place; read arcs require and expose tokens to the lambda/kernel but do NOT consume them; inhibitor arcs prevent firing when the source place has at least the weight indicated and are NOT present in the lambda or kernel `input`.

items.description: Input arc from a place or component port into a transition.

inputArcs.description: Input arcs that gate transition firing. Standard arcs consume tokens, read arcs observe tokens without consuming them, and inhibitor arcs block firing based on token counts.

placeId.description: Legacy shorthand for a normal output place endpoint. Prefer `endpoint` for new data.

endpoint.description: Output endpoint. Use `kind: "componentPort"` to produce tokens into a component instance port.

placeId.description: ID of a place in the same net as the transition.

componentInstanceId.description: ID of a component instance in the same net as the transition.

portPlaceId.description: ID of a place marked `isPort: true` in the component instance's referenced subnet.

weight.description: Number of tokens produced into the output place.

items.description: Output arc from a transition into a place or component port.

outputArcs.description: Output arcs that receive tokens after this transition fires.

lambdaType.description: Use predicate for boolean enabling logic when transition lambda authoring is available; use stochastic for rate-based firing when stochasticity is available.

lambdaCode.description: Optional function body ending in `return`, with `input` and `parameters` ambient (the legacy `export default Lambda((input, parameters) => …)` module form is also accepted). Lambda code is meaningful only when stochasticity is enabled OR when colours are enabled and the transition has at least one standard or read input arc from a coloured place. `input` is keyed by INPUT PLACE NAME (PascalCase) for coloured standard and read arcs, and the value is a tuple sized to that arc's weight (weight 2 means a 2-token array). Read arc tokens are present in `input` but are not consumed when the transition fires. Inhibitor arcs and uncoloured input places are NOT present in `input`. Each token is an object keyed by the colour type's element names (e.g. `{ x, y, velocity }`). `parameters` is keyed by each parameter's `variableName` value (lower_snake_case, e.g. `parameters.infection_rate`). Predicate lambdas MUST return a boolean (true = enabled given these tokens, false = disabled). Stochastic lambdas MUST return a non-negative number = expected firings per simulation second (0 disables, Infinity always fires). Lambda is called per token combination satisfying arc weights, so it MUST be deterministic — put randomness in the transition kernel, not here. Leave empty when lambda authoring is unavailable; the runtime supplies the always-enabled default.

transitionKernelCode.description: Optional function body ending in `return`, with `input` and `parameters` ambient (the legacy `export default TransitionKernel((input, parameters) => …)` module form is also accepted). Transition kernel code is meaningful only when colours are enabled and the transition has at least one coloured output place. `input` and `parameters` have the same shape as the transition's lambda. MUST return an object keyed by OUTPUT PLACE NAME with a tuple sized to that arc's weight. Coloured output places MUST be present; uncoloured output places MUST be omitted (they are auto-populated with empty tokens). Token attribute values must match the output type: real/integer use numbers, boolean uses booleans. When stochasticity is enabled, `real` attributes may also use `Distribution.Gaussian(mean, sd)` / `Distribution.Uniform(min, max)` / `Distribution.Lognormal(mu, sigma)` (discrete attributes always take plain values); each distribution is sampled once per token, and chained `.map(fn)` calls on the same distribution share that single sample. Leave empty when no coloured outputs exist.

items.description: A Petri net transition. Transitions connect places and define firing logic.

id.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

description.description: Optional human-readable summary shown to users.

iconSlug.description: Short icon identifier used by the UI for this colour/type. Typical values are `"circle"` or `"square"`; the UI defaults to `"circle"`.

displayColor.description: CSS colour string for the UI badge, e.g. `"#1E90FF"` or `"rgb(30,144,255)"`.

elementId.description: Stable identifier for this colour element.

name.description: Token attribute identifier used DIRECTLY in code. Lambdas, kernels, dynamics, visualizers, and metrics destructure tokens as `{ <name> }`, so this must be a valid JavaScript identifier (e.g. `machine_damage_ratio`, `x`, `velocity`). Spaces, hyphens, and leading digits will break user code that references the attribute; prefer lower_snake_case for consistency with parameter naming.

type.description: `real` is continuous and may be updated by dynamics. `integer`, `boolean`, `uuid`, and `string` are discrete token attributes updated by transition kernels. `integer` values are stored as Float64 and rounded on read/write: they are exact only within ±2^53 (±9,007,199,254,740,992); values beyond that lose precision silently. `uuid` is a 128-bit RFC 4122 identifier: runtime code sees it as a `bigint`, frame buffers store it as two little-endian 64-bit lanes, and at-rest data (documents, scenarios) uses canonical lowercase strings. `uuid` fields are OPTIONAL in kernel outputs — omitted values are auto-generated deterministically from the seeded simulation RNG — and non-UUID inputs are converted deterministically via UUIDv5. `string` is variable-length text, compared by value: runtime code sees plain JS strings, and each distinct value is stored once per run via interning — frame buffers hold 64-bit pool references. Kernels and markings write `string` values (missing values become the empty string); dynamics can read but never update them.

items.description: One typed attribute on a coloured token.

elements.description: Typed token attributes available on tokens of this colour/type. Element order matters: coloured initial state in scenario per_place mode supplies rows in this order.

items.description: A coloured-token type. Coloured places store token objects with these attributes.

types.description: Token types local to this subnet.

id.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

anyOf.description: Stable identifier for an SDCPN entity, a UUID. Use unique IDs within the net. Any other string is converted to a stable UUID, so the same string always names the same entity.

colorId.description: ID of the colour/type whose token attributes this dynamics function updates. MUST match the `colorId` of every place that lists this equation in `dynamics`.

code.description: Function body ending in `return`, with the input and `parameters` ambient (the module form `export default Dynamics((token, parameters) => …)`, with one parameter per coupled token, is also accepted). With `arity` 1 the input is `token`, ONE token of THIS place (`return { level: -token.level };`), and `tokens` is NOT defined. With `arity` 2 and above the input is `tokens`, a tuple of exactly `arity` tokens of THIS place (`const [a, b] = tokens;`). Neither is all tokens of the place, and neither holds other places' tokens. MUST return real-valued derivatives (i.e. dx/dt, NOT the new value): one record for arity 1, an array of `arity` records (one per token, in order) above that. Integer and boolean elements are discrete and remain unchanged by dynamics. `parameters` is keyed by each parameter's `variableName` value (lower_snake_case, e.g. `parameters.damage_per_second`).

arity.description: How many tokens the equation couples, from 1 to 8. The simulator applies the code to every unordered combination of that many distinct tokens of the place, in index order, and sums the contributions into each token's derivative: 1 is a per-token equation (the usual case), 2 a pairwise interaction such as an attraction between every two tokens.

items.description: A differential equation for continuous dynamics on coloured tokens. The `colorId` MUST match the colour of every place that lists this equation in `dynamics`, and returned derivatives only update that colour's real-valued elements.

differentialEquations.description: Differential equations local to this subnet.

variableName.description: lower_snake_case identifier used DIRECTLY in user code as `parameters.<value>` (e.g. `parameters.crash_threshold`, NOT `parameters.crashThreshold`). Must start with a lowercase letter; only `[a-z0-9_]` allowed.

type.description: Primitive parameter type. Real and integer values use numeric strings; boolean values use the literal strings `"true"` and `"false"`.

defaultValue.description: Default parameter value as a plain string: numeric for real/integer parameters (e.g. `"3"`, `"0.05"`) and `"true"` or `"false"` for booleans. Expressions are NOT supported here — use scenario `parameterOverrides` for expressions.

name: hash_query_entities
description: Read entities from the HASH graph, as the signed-in user: only what they may see is returned, and archived entities are never returned, so an entity that is absent may exist but be hidden from them, archived, or filed under another type title or web. Filters combine: an entity must match every filter given. Returns compact text: first candidate property definitions matched by returned keys, each qualified by propertyTypeId (a versioned URL), with its title and description (units are in the description; cut short when long). Multiple versions are alternatives; this global legend does not determine which definition applies to any entity or value. Key matches alone do not establish property ownership, including within opaque JSON. No unit conversion is inferred. Then each entity type title with its entityTypeId (a versioned URL); then each entity, headed by its types' titles (each with its entityTypeId when two types in the read share that title), its name (cut short when long), and (linked) if it was reached by following links rather than matching the filters, or (draft); then its entityId (`<webId>~<uuid>`, with `~<draftId>` for a draft), editionId (the exact version read), for a link entity the entityIds it links from and to, and one line per property. A property's short name, here and in nested values, comes from its base URL, unless two properties in the read would share one: then both show by their full base URL, so a name holds within one read only. A large value is summarised as <kind, size: shape>; to see it, read the entity again by entityIds with its id in fullValuesFor. The graph returns at most 1,000 matches at once; when it stopped there, the text says more may match than shown, so narrow the filter. A read that failed returns { error }. Read webs with hash_query_webs first, for the web ids to filter by; then read the types of the entities found with hash_query_entity_types, by their entityTypeIds, for the links and other properties a type allows, and follow up on a found entity by its entityId.

entityTypes.description: Entity type titles to match, for example `Organization`. A title matches every type with that title, in any web and at any version; a versioned entityTypeId matches that type version only. Entities of any listed type match.

webIds.description: Web ids to read from. An entity belongs to the web of the user or organization that owns it.

entityIds.description: Entity ids to read, for example ids returned by an earlier read: `webId~entityUuid`, or `webId~entityUuid~draftId` for a draft. An id with a draft part reads that draft.

traversalDepth.description: How many links to follow from the matched entities, at most 3. Each link is followed in either direction, so mixed chains such as A → B ← C are included; a matched link entity's own endpoints are included too. 0 returns only the matches. Defaults to 1.

includeDrafts.description: Whether to include draft entities. Defaults to false. An entity id with a draft part reads that draft either way, along with reached draft links whose left or right endpoint is an explicitly named draft. This exception does not include other draft endpoint records or recursively include further draft links; link endpoint ids remain intact.

fullValuesFor.description: Entity ids whose property values to show in full, as JSON, where the result would otherwise summarise a large value. It doesn't change which entities are read: read them by entityIds too.

name: hash_query_entity_types
description: List the entity types in the HASH graph that the signed-in user can see: the versions named by entityTypeIds, or else each type's latest version. Filters combine: a type must match every filter given. Returns compact text: each type headed by its title and entityTypeId (a versioned URL), then its description (cut short when long), its properties (inherited ones included), each by its short name and its title, and its links, each by its title and linkEntityTypeId, with the entity types it may point to (any, when not limited). A type's title or entityTypeId can filter an entity read. The graph returns at most 1,000 types at once; when it stopped there, the text says more may match than shown. A read that failed returns { error }. Read it after hash_query_webs and hash_query_entities, for the entityTypeIds the entities found carry. Pass the entityTypeIds of entities you read; webIds rarely help, since most types live in HASH's shared webs. Without filters it lists the entity types the user can see, up to that limit: a very large read.

entityTypeIds.description: Entity types to read, each a versioned URL as an entity's entityTypeIds name it, for example from hash_query_entities. Those exact versions are read.

webIds.description: Web ids whose own entity types to list. Most types live in HASH's shared webs, not the user's or their organizations'.

name: hash_query_webs
description: List the signed-in user's own HASH web and the webs of the organizations they belong to. Returns compact text, one line per web: its kind (user or organization), its name and @shortname where it has them, and its webId. A web id can limit an entity or entity type read. A read that failed returns { error }. Read it first, before hash_query_entities and hash_query_entity_types.

name: app_save_net
description: Save the net open in the editor to HASH as a new version, exactly as the editor's Save button does; others who can see the net then see that version. The net open in the editor is documentId "net-42". Call it only when the user asks for a save or agrees to one you offered. The user approves each save on a card; it saves the net as the editor holds it then, with every unsaved edit, the user's and yours. It saves only the net: this conversation and its Ledger stay in Brunch and are not saved into HASH. Returns { saved: true, decisionTime, title, stillDirty } when saved: decisionTime is the saved version's time, and stillDirty means edits made since are not in it. Returns { saved: false, error, note } when the page could not confirm the save, and fails with an error carrying the same note when the page's answer was lost: The save is not confirmed: a version may or may not have been written. Tell the user, who can check the version list, and don't call app_save_net again until they ask. Returns { saved: false, reason } when it did not start (the user declined, the net is read-only or unsaved, it has no unsaved changes, a save is already in progress, or it isn't the open net): nothing was saved. If it is refused because the document changed since your last view of the net, read the net, then call it again.

documentId.description: The ID of the net open in the editor, given in this tool's description.

name: ledger_query_basis
description: Use when the USER asks why a visible net element exists or is modelled as it is, instead of answering from memory. Finds the element in the latest net read, or in the net read back after a later change, and returns its recorded basis: the reflections that name the element and, behind them, the claims, entities and discharged obligations they rest on, each with its ID, and the conversation turns those records came from, each with its ID and the opening of the USER's words. Answer from that basis and cite its record IDs. Cite every returned turn too, by quoting the opening of the USER's words, never by its ID, so the USER can see what they said that the answer rests on. A claim under `superseded` was later replaced: say so, and give its replacement. It also lists the canonical calls that changed the element, with their document and Ledger revisions. A basis-absent disposition means no reflection names the element: say plainly that its basis was not recorded rather than reconstructing one. You may point to related records, but do not offer a rationale of your own for it. A stale-read disposition means the net changed after the latest net view, a read or a change's read-back, without a later read-back: read it again, then query.
